text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Insurance giant National Mutual Holdings made a powerful debut on the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, trading more than 35 million shares worth A$62 million and delivering almost 600,000 investors big profits when institutions pushed NatMut's shares 7 per cent above the issue price. Page 1.

Telecommunications giant Optus Vision, yesterday agreed to prop up the ailing Australian Rugby League with an estimated A$100 million rescue package. The move by Optus is a hit back at News Ltd's rival Super League competition which received the go-ahead from the Federal Court last Friday. Page

Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot has warned the Coalition's controversial Workplace Relations Bill will not pass into law without significant amendments. Kernot made her first statement about the Bill claiming that after 30 hours of negotiations with
the Government no agreement had been reached. Page 3.

According to a recent study by The Economist Intelligence Unit, many multinational corporations are finding it hard to justify investment in Australia. It was revealed that many multinationals felt Australia was becoming less significant on the world stage and suffered from a lack of relevant industry policy. Page 5.

Mining giant WMC Ltd has made 445 workers redundant as it appointed contractors to operate in its West Australian gold and nickel mines. The move signals the beginning-of-the-end of the large company-employed workforce in the West Australian mining industy. Page 21.

A cross-shareholding deal between Solomon Lew's Premier Investments Ltd and Rodney Adler's FAI Insurances Ltd will be reversed following the announcement by Premier that it will buy back FAI's 14.7 per cent stake in the company. The deal, as a part hangover from th controversial Yannon
affair, also comes after Premier's decision to sell its A$33 million stake in FAI last Friday. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Heavyweight life insurer National Mutual Holdings Ltd, the first Australian life insurer to demutualise and list on the Australian Stock Exchange, burst onto the ASX yesterday trading as the country's thirtieth biggest company, with strong domestic and international demand for its shares pushing its market capitalisation past A$3 billion. Page 31.

At the first annual meeting since the full privatisation of the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, senior management yesterday predicted a flat profit this year and a drop in official interest rates before Christmas - and warned that household indebtedness apeared to be increasing. Page 31.

A report sponsored by the London-based Economist magazine entitled 'Australia's Foreign Investment Challenge' has accused Australian Governments and Government departments of having incoherent and inconsistent industry policies which have discouraged overeas investors from coming to Australia. Page 31.

As Victorian TAB turnover continues to fall following their agencies' loss last week of the Sky Channel racing signal, Tabcorp Holdings Ltd is believed to have told several of its agencies they will be closed, a move feared to be the first step in a ratioalisation which will see the State's 290 TAB outlets cut by more than 50 per cent. Page 31.

According to the latest quarterly DHL-Gallup export indicator survey, almost a quarter of Australia's exporters are now looking at the Middle East as their main target for new business in the year ahead, with 24 per cent deeming the Middle East to be thei primary target for new business. Page 33.

Optus Communications chairman Russell Fynmore told a Committee for the Economic Development of Australia function in Melbourne yesterday, Optus' much maligned overhead cabling and mobile phone towers would play a key role in further telecommunications cometition. Page 33.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Optus Vision's decision to provide the Australian Rugby League with a further A$120 million, making Optus' total commitment to the ARL A$210 million, has caused more problems for the A$4.5 billion float of Optus Communications, already suffering from bickring between shareholders. Page 29.

At yesterday's Commonwealth Bank annual meeting, shareholders approved a share giveaway to bank staff that will cut another A$52 million off profits over the next three years. The plan will give between 66 and 75 per cent of the bank's employees A$1,000 worth of shares a year, free, for three years. Page 29.

CanWest Global Communications, the Ten Network's major shareholder with a 57 per cent economic interest in the television network, is looking to scuttle plans for fellow Ten shareholders to sell their shares to a unit trust by forming a
separate company t deal through the Macquarie Bank. Page 29.

National Mutual, Australia's second largest life insurance group, joined the ranks of the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, making a stunning debut which saw a A$510 million return to the 564,000-plus shareholders who took advantage of a decision to deutualise. Page 29.

Cambridge Gulf Exploration executive deputy chairman Brian Conway is facing Corporations Law charges over a statement to the stockmarket in December 1993 which detailed the recovery of six carats of diamonds and forecast potential annual profits of $A1.74 billion. Conway has been charged by summons with making false or misleading statements. Page 31.

In a move which tightens Premier Investments capital base and ends a sometimes uncomfortable relationship, Premier, headed by Solomon Lew, plans to buy and cancel the FAI group's 14.7 per cent stake in the company for A$8.6 million. Page 31.
THE AGE

The debut of insurance group National Mutual Holdings on the stockmarket was regarded as impressive, with NMH delivering A$510 million in instant profits to over 564,000 shareholders who took advantage of the group's decision to demutualise. National Mutul Holdings started the day with A$2.55 billion worth of market capitalisation and by the end of trading, the figure had leapt to A$3.06 billion. Page C1.

Commonwealth Bank shareholders have ignored the prediction of "flat" profits for the banking giant and have approved a share give-away to 36,000 employees of a A$52 million package which will see staff inherit A$1000 worth of Commonwealth Bank shares a yer for three years. Page C1.

In the wake of the National Mutual Holdings listing, the Australian Stock Exchange estimates that the number of Australians who own shares has risen substantially from the 2.5 million listed in 1994. The ASX estimates 23 per cent of Australians currently old shares, with a significant proportion
being "small time" investors. Page C1.

Melbourne's courts may see the end of another public business battle with former Coles-Myer director Solomon Lew expected to review the legal action mounted against Coles Myer and the Australian Securities Commission after the Lew camp gained access to ASC documents which could prompt a settlement. Page 1.

The pending A$4.5 billion float of Optus Communications has been set back following a fallout between industrial shareholders and the float organisers and the decision by its pay-TV offshoot, Optus Vision, to invest A$120 million into the Australian RugbyLeague. Page C3.

John Conomos, a senior executive with Toyota Australia, warned that the company's planned A$600 million a year export program could be adversely affected if the Federal Government scrapped the export subsidy for the car industry. Conomos' comments came folowing the US complaint to the World Trade
Organisation about the Australian export facilitation scheme. Page C3.
